title: What Is the Largest Desert in the World? (Hint: Not the Sahara)
caption:
The biggest desert on Earth isn't the Sahara. It's Antarctica.

A desert is defined by how little precipitation falls, not by heat or sand. One common rule: under 250 mm a year.
Antarctica's polar plateau gets about 50 mm. Its desert covers 13.96 million km², the Arctic about 13.7 million.
The Sahara, at 8.6 million km², is still the largest hot desert.

caption:

Each hour of the day is 12,500 years.
Farming starts about 58 minutes before midnight.
Writing: about 25 minutes before midnight.
The Industrial Revolution: the last 77 seconds.

607 submarine cable systems are in service, with 102 more planned (TeleGeography, Sep 2026).

The ITU says they carry more than 99% of international data traffic. Satellites carry just 0.37% of US international capacity.

title: How Much Would Sea Level Rise If Antarctica Melted? (Bedmap3 Data)
caption:
If all of Antarctica's ice melted, global sea level would rise about 58 metres.

The ice sheet holds 27.17 million km³ of ice, on average 1,948 m thick (Bedmap3 survey).
At its thickest it reaches 4,757 m, and under the grounded ice 47% of the bedrock lies below sea level.
It holds roughly 61% of all the fresh water on Earth.
